title: Lambda Concurrent Execution Limits and Throttling

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.5.3 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.5.3 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" (metric_name="ConcurrentExecutions" OR metric_name="Throttles")
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.3_lambda_concurrent_execut_3"
| sort -_time
description: Account- and function-level concurrency caps cause synchronous throttles and async retries; monitoring utilization prevents dropped work during traffic spikes.
value: Detecting lambda concurrent execution limits and throttling early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest `ConcurrentExecutions`, `Throttles`, and reserved concurrency settings (from tags or a nightly inventory lookup). Compare concurrent usage to reserved and account limits. Alert on any non-zero throttles or when concurrent executions approach the configured cap for bursty functions.
visualization: Line chart (ConcurrentExecutions vs limit by function), Single value (throttle count), Area chart (stacked concurrency by function).
knownFalsePositives: Planned load tests, new regions, and one-off batch jobs can legitimately run near limits. We treat a breach as normal when it is tied to a change ticket and a known window, and we reset after the window ends.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest `ConcurrentExecutions`, `Throttles`, and reserved concurrency settings (from tags or a nightly inventory lookup). Compare concurrent usage to reserved and account limits. Alert on any non-zero throttles or when concurrent executions approach the configured cap for bursty functions.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" (metric_name="ConcurrentExecutions" OR metric_name="Throttles")
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.3_lambda_concurrent_execut_3"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect lambda concurrent execution limits and throttling. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_3_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (ConcurrentExecutions vs limit by function), Single value (throttle count), Area chart (stacked concurrency by function)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of lambda concurrent execution limits and throttling so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
